extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of coal combustion residual (CCR) units, environmental compliance managers, consulting hydrogeologists/engineers, P.E.s, analytical laboratories, and state/EPA regulators
extracted.subtask_short: groundwater monitoring for legacy CCR impoundments
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and technical expectations for design, installation, sampling, analysis, reporting, and corrective action of groundwater monitoring systems at legacy CCR (coal combustion residual) surface impoundments. Covers monitoring well network design, sampling/statistical plans, deadlines, reporting, corrective action timelines, and closure/post-closure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring well network minimums and representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Install a network of upgradient and downgradient monitoring wells that yields groundwater samples from the uppermost aquifer that accurately represent background groundwater quality and groundwater passing the downgradient waste boundary, monitoring all potential contaminant pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation requires a minimum of one upgradient and three downgradient wells (40 CFR 257.91(a)(1)–(2)), but exact number, location, and depth are site-specific. Number/placement must be determined based on thorough characterization including aquifer thickness, groundwater flow rate and direction (including seasonal/temporal fluctuations), and geological and hydrogeological site conditions. The number and placement are critical for proper groundwater characterization (see 80 FR 21399).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring well construction, operation, and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring wells must be cased, constructed, operated, and maintained to preserve borehole integrity, screened interval, and other components so the well performs to design specifications throughout the monitoring system life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators must protect wells from activities that may damage them (e.g., livestock, vehicles, machinery). Maintain wells to ensure sampling yields representative data and performance is preserved over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and professional/state certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Design, installation, development, and decommissioning of any aspect of the groundwater monitoring system must be thoroughly documented and included in the operating record, and the system must be certified by a P.E. or approved by the Participating State Director or EPA as meeting §257.91 standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects owners/operators to include full documentation in the operating record and obtain P.E. certification or state/EPA approval that the monitoring system complies with regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater sampling and analysis program content
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner/operator must develop a sampling and analysis program that satisfies §257.93 and includes the monitoring network list, sampling schedule, sampling procedures and techniques, sample preservation and shipping protocols, analytical procedures including an appropriate statistical method, and quality assurance/quality control methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must include all analytes listed in Appendix III and Appendix IV. EPA guidance (e.g., RCRA Groundwater Monitoring: Draft Technical Guidance, Low-Flow Ground-Water Sampling Procedures) contains recommendations for analytical procedures, QA/QC controls, and sampling protocols. Statistical procedures for evaluating monitoring data must be selected and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined detection and assessment monitoring (simultaneous Appendix III & IV sampling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample and analyze constituents listed in Appendix IV at the same time as those in Appendix III (combined detection and assessment monitoring) for legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining Appendix III and IV accelerates identification of constituents of concern and initiation of corrective action; it collects all information detection monitoring would collect while providing more data to understand fate/transport and correlations. EPA acknowledges increased lab throughput but considers logistics (no extra field mobilizations) manageable. Facilities must still be able to evaluate SSIs and SSLs with combined data. Concerns about losing critical detection-monitoring data are unsubstantiated because Appendix III data are still collected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate Source Demonstrations (ASD) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: ASDs should only be accepted where there is a strong technical case that an alternate source, not the CCR unit, caused a constituent exceedance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technically weak or equivocal ASDs should be rejected expeditiously to avoid unnecessary delays in corrective action. If an alternate source explains Appendix III exceedances and also explains Appendix IV SSLs, a single ASD may cover both; otherwise, combined monitoring reduces the likelihood of missing Appendix IV exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline — single compliance date for groundwater monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: All groundwater monitoring requirements for legacy CCR surface impoundments must be completed no later than Monday, May 10, 2027 (30 months from the effective date of the final rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA established a single deadline (extended from proposed split deadlines) to accommodate laboratory capacity, sampling independence concerns, and seasonal variability while ensuring timely initiation of monitoring and corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline sampling — eight independent samples per well
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must complete sampling and analysis of a minimum of eight independent samples for each background and downgradient well (as required by §257.94(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalizes the requirement that the eight baseline samples be collected no later than May 10, 2027. Commenters' concerns about feasibility, sample independence, lab backlogs, and seasonal variability were considered in setting the single extended deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frequency and statistical independence considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling and analysis plans must account for the need to collect statistically independent baseline samples and consider seasonal variability; sampling plans cannot reasonably be completed prior to baseline sample collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too frequent sampling risks autocorrelated baseline samples that undermine required statistical analyses. EPA acknowledges lab backlogs and third-party availability may affect timelines and built flexibility into deadlines. Sampling schedules should be designed to avoid non-independence and to capture seasonal groundwater variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action report requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must prepare annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action reports in accordance with §257.90(e), due January 31 following establishment of the monitoring system and annually thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must document monitoring activities and corrective action progress, and include maps/aerial images/diagrams of the CCR unit and all upgradient/downgradient wells; identification of wells installed or decommissioned; monitoring data (§§257.90–257.98); narrative discussion of transitions between monitoring programs; tabulated groundwater level data; validation of well locations vs measured flow directions; appendices with raw data (boring logs, well installation diagrams, field sampling data sheets, laboratory analytical data including QA/QC and data validation). Reports must be organized so compliance is evident, supporting data are easy to locate, and the public can readily review the data. The report must be posted to the unit's public CCR website with a clear, printable/downloadable filename.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of well locations and groundwater flow directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Upgradient and downgradient well locations and depths should be validated annually with respect to measured and mapped groundwater flow directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual validation helps ensure wells remain representative given seasonal/temporal changes; include tabulated and analyzed groundwater level data to confirm or determine flow directions and assess residual CCR left in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggering corrective action and required corrective action program
rubrics_metrics.description: If monitoring demonstrates exceedance of groundwater protection standards (GWPS) for Appendix IV constituents, corrective action is required per §§257.96–257.98 throughout the active life and post-closure care period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrective action program includes initiating an Assessment of Corrective Measures (ACM) to prevent further releases, remediate releases, and restore affected areas (§257.96(a)). After ACM completion, the owner/operator must select a remedy that attains GWPS (§257.97(a),(b)). Implementation of remedial activities must begin within 90 days of remedy selection (§257.98(a)). Implementing source control (e.g., closure by removal) may commence remedy implementation but does not negate the requirement to implement the groundwater remediation portion within the schedule established in the remedy selection report.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACM and remedy selection timelines and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiate ACM within 90 days of determining a statistically significant level (SSL) has occurred and complete the ACM within another 90 days; an extension not to exceed 60 days may be warranted for site-specific conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This results in a timeline of 180 to 240 days after determining an SSL to complete the ACM and select a remedy; EPA did not change these deadlines in this rulemaking. EPA expects facilities to have sufficient site characterization and information to assess corrective measures within these timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for remedy selection
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing corrective measures and selecting a remedy, owners/operators must consider impacts on nearest surface water bodies and nearest private/public groundwater supply wells, and account for public input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public meeting must be held and community input considered before selecting a remedy. Remedy selection may include closure by removal as source control, but groundwater remediation components must still be implemented on the schedule in the remedy selection report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of closure and post-closure requirements and closure initiation deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply existing closure and post-closure care requirements (§§257.101–257.104) to legacy CCR surface impoundments (except alternative closure §257.103(f)); require initiation of closure within 12 months of the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects most legacy CCR surface impoundments are unlined and therefore must close. Alternative closure provisions are inappropriate for inactive legacy impoundments that cannot demonstrate need to continue unit use.
